rationale: This is a component swap on the already-tested "Inventory-Cash Coverage Imbalance" (invt/act minus a liquidity term) and is further mechanically redundant because wcap/act = 1 − lct/act, so the signal collapses to inventory intensity plus current-liability intensity, ground already covered by three archived inventory-liquidity signals.

A simple but coherent and internally consistent scaled-intangible-growth test whose negative sign follows the investment/asset-growth logic; it is close to the archived DELTA(capx/sale) construction applied to a genuinely different asset class, though the sales denominator makes it partly a sales-decline signal and coverage will be thin.

This restates the archived "Cash-Constrained Replacement Shortfall" with the funding leg swapped from oancf to Δre and MIN swapped for SUB, and because Δre/at is essentially retained profitability, the subtracted leg injects the well-known profitability anomaly rather than testing a new replacement-strain mechanism.

Algebraically this is just the additive version of the archived "Short-Funded Fixed-Asset Build" (SUB of the negated second leg equals the sum of the same two components), i.e., a pure operator swap on a signal whose long-short alpha ran opposite to the hypothesized sign.

The NEG(ABS(capx − implied depreciation)) term is a genuinely non-monotonic and novel "steady-state maintenance" construct rather than a repackaged investment level, though the Δre/at leg loads a known profitability effect and the MIN over a sharply skewed absolute-deviation score risks a long leg driven mostly by retained-earnings growth.

The interaction of investment instability with a thin accumulated-earnings base is economically coherent and consistently signed, but the equal-weighted subtraction of re/at risks the signal degenerating into a familiar distress/quality proxy, so the marginal contribution of the capex-volatility leg should be checked directly.
